analysis_steps.goal: Model SZE energetics using thermal and kinematic SZE conical bubble models

method.value: Rowe & Silk (2011) self-similar wind bubble solution modified for conical outflow

evidence.quote: We base our treatment of the expansion of the wind bubble on the model in RS11, which uses the self-similar stellar wind bubble solution of Weaver et al. (1977).

key_parameters.value: Decrement -25.9 uJy (primary beam corrected), Delta T_b = -37.7 uK

evidence.quote: The peak brightness of the SZE decrement of $-$25.9 $\mu$Jy (Section 2.1) corresponds to a brightness temperature change of $\Delta T_{\rm b,peak} = -37.7$ $\mu$K.

assumptions.value: Conical wind geometry with half-angle 30 deg, inclination 45 deg to line of sight

evidence.quote: we assume that our observed SZE signal comes from a region which is a spherical cone, with the cone apex and the center of curvature located at the QSO. We estimate the half angle of the cone in our system to be $\theta = 30^{\circ}$
We further assume that the axis of the outflow is at an angle of 45$^{\circ}$ to the outward extension of our line of sight.

fitting.value: Analytic inversion of two equations for outer radius and maximum Compton y

evidence.quote: Equations (3) and (4) are two relations with two unknowns. Since we have observed values for both $R \approx 112$ kpc (corrected for projection) and $y_{\rm max} \approx 2.08 \times 10^{-5}$, we can estimate both $L_W$ and $t$

validation.value: Consistency across enthalpy, pure tSZE, and tSZE+kSZE energy estimates

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the fair agreement in the total energy estimate between the three different methods (total enthalpy, tSZE only and kSZE+tSZE) suggests that our estimate of that quantity at least is fairly robust.

findings_qualitative.value: Extended optical/NIR emission line gas aligns with the position angle of the SZE decrement, corroborating a broad outflow cone.

evidence.quote: The SZE detection is corroborated by the presence of extended emission line gas at the same position angle as the wind.

evidence.loc: 3.1 The quasar host galaxy and its environment
evidence.quote: Taken together with the SZE detection, we hypothesize that C1 and C2 help to define a broad outflow cone

findings_qualitative.value: The long cooling time (~0.6 Gyr) indicates thermal wind bubbles can provide feedback between episodic bursts of quasar activity.

evidence.quote: the age we estimate for the bubble, $\sim 0.1$ Gyr, and the long cooling time, $\sim 0.6$ Gyr, means that such bubbles may be effective at providing feedback between bursts of quasar activity.

claims.hypothesis: Quasar thermal winds blow bubbles into the IGM that produce a detectable SZE decrement
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 4 continuum observations with compact configuration and uv-tapering after subtracting point sources
claims.result: Detected a flux decrement of -23.1 uJy (-25.9 uJy after 12% primary beam correction) at 3.5 sigma significance SW of the quasar
claims.finding: First direct detection of an SZE bubble produced by a quasar wind

evidence.quote: In this letter, we present evidence that we have made the first detection of such a bubble, associated with the hyperluminous quasar HE 0515-4414.
recovers an apparent dip of flux density of $-23.1\,\mu$Jy, significant at the 3.5$\sigma$ level, to the SW of the quasar position.

claims.hypothesis: The asymmetry (one-sidedness) of the SZE decrement can be explained by kinematic SZE effects
claims.experiment: Analytical modeling of tSZE and kSZE contributions to the decrement
claims.result: In the combined model, ~60% of the decrement is kSZE and 40% is tSZE
claims.finding: The one-sided nature of the SZE signal is explained by combined thermal and kinetic SZE where approaching counter-flow components cancel

evidence.quote: a combined tSZE and kSZE model provides a natural explanation for the one-sided appearance. In the receding half of the outflow (relative to the observer) the kZSE and tSZE contributions to the SZE are both of the same sign, but in the approaching half the two partially cancel.

claims.hypothesis: Quasar wind kinetic luminosity matches standard theoretical predictions of 1-10% bolometric luminosity
claims.experiment: Comparison of derived wind kinetic energy and luminosity to quasar bolometric and accretion energy
claims.result: Wind luminosity is ~0.003% of bolometric luminosity and E_W / (eta M_BH c^2) ~ 0.01%
claims.finding: The wind kinetic luminosity is at the lower end of theoretical models (~0.01% of bolometric/accretion power vs 1-10% predicted)

evidence.quote: Although the wind luminosity seen in HE0515-4414 is high in absolute terms, it is only a small fraction ($\approx 0.003$%) of the bolometric luminosity of the quasar ($\approx 1.3\times 10^{15}L_{\odot}$).
This fraction, $E_{\rm W}/(\eta M_{\bullet} c^2)\approx 0.01$% (0.02% if the wind is two-sided), is still low compared to the models.

why_this_data.value: HE 0515-4414 was chosen as the most luminous radio-quiet quasar with good ALMA visibility to maximize the expected SZE signal.

evidence.quote: We selected the most luminous radio-quiet quasar we could find in the literature that had good visibility to ALMA, HE 0515-4414 ($z=1.71$; Reimers et al. 1998).

why_this_method.value: ALMA Band 4 was chosen because the peak intensity of the thermal SZE decrement occurs at ~130 GHz.

evidence.quote: The peak intensity of the thermal SZE decrement is seen at $\approx 130$ GHz (Sunyaev & Zeldovich 1972), which lies in ALMA band-4.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Contamination from an intracluster medium or intragroup medium ruled out based on small cluster mass and lack of obvious groups/clusters in Spitzer/Gemini/HST imaging.

evidence.loc: 3.1 The quasar host galaxy and its environment
evidence.quote: The estimated mass of this cluster, $6\times 10^{12}M_{\odot}$ is much too small for it to contribute to the observed SZE though.

evidence.loc: 3.1 The quasar host galaxy and its environment
evidence.quote: The lack of any other obvious group or cluster in the field argues against significant contamination of the SZE signal by the intracluster medium of a compact cluster or intragroup medium

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Starburst-driven wind considered as an alternative origin, requiring SFR ~ 500 M_sun/yr for 1.3e8 yr; cannot be ruled out without SFR constraints.

evidence.quote: Given the relatively low power of the wind, it is also worth investigating whether it can be produced by a starburst in the quasar host galaxy... In the absence of constraints on the star formation rate in this object, we cannot currently rule out a starburst origin.

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot rule out a starburst-driven wind origin due to lack of star formation rate constraints.

evidence.quote: In the absence of constraints on the star formation rate in this object, we cannot currently rule out a starburst origin.

limitations_admitted.value: Results are based on a single object and need confirmation in the broader quasar population.

evidence.quote: We emphasize though that this is only a single object, and that studies of further objects are needed to confirm this in the general quasar population.

limitations_admitted.value: Strong shock assumption may not be valid if the quasar resides in a massive halo (>~ 1e13 M_sun).

evidence.quote: in this model, the shock speed is relatively low ($\approx 500\;$kms$^{-1}$), and it is possible that if the quasar is in a sufficiently massive virialized dark matter halo ($\stackrel{>}{_{\sim}}10^{13} M_{\odot}$) with a sound speed comparable to the estimated shock speed, the assumption of a strong shock may not be valid.

referee_caveats_inferred: The 3.5-sigma decrement detection is modest and reliant on uv-tapering and accurate uv-subtraction of four point sources.
The physical interpretation relies heavily on geometric cone assumptions (opening angle 30 deg, inclination 45 deg) and strong shock approximations.
